fields.short_description: Fuel level is too low, High voltage battery assembly failure, High voltage battery is not sufficiently charged
fields.detailed_technical_explanation: Code P3000 (Fuel level is too low, High voltage battery assembly failure, High voltage battery is not sufficiently charged) sets when the overall HV bus voltage - measured system-wide rather than at any single battery pack or contactor - reads outside its expected window or fails an ECM performance check. Because this is a system-level measurement, causes span a genuinely low/high pack state of charge, a contactor not fully seating, or a fault in the HV bus voltage-sense circuit itself rather than any single named component.

fields.short_description: Long Term Fuel Trim Bank 1 System Too Lean
fields.detailed_technical_explanation: Code P1128 (Long Term Fuel Trim Bank 1 System Too Lean) sets when overall short- or long-term fuel trim for a bank moves outside its normal operating window without a specific lean or rich bias being isolated. Causes span vacuum leaks, a fuel delivery imbalance, or a fuel/air metering sensor reading incorrectly for that bank.

fields.fix_title: Check HV battery state of charge
fields.step_by_step_instructions: 1. Verify the HV system is de-energized and locked out per the manufacturer's procedure before any inspection • 2. Read HV battery state of charge on a scan tool • 3. Charge the pack to a normal operating range if low • 4. Clear the code and recheck bus voltage at a normal state of charge

fields.fix_title: Inspect main HV contactors for full seating
fields.step_by_step_instructions: 1. Verify the HV system is de-energized and locked out per the manufacturer's procedure, then confirm zero volts with a rated meter • 2. Inspect the main positive/negative contactors for feedback confirming full seating • 3. Test contactor operation per the manufacturer's procedure • 4. Repair or replace a contactor found not seating fully

Inspect the bus voltage-sense wiring and connectors for damage or corrosion • 3. Repair or replace the sense circuit as needed • 4. Restore the HV system per procedure and clear the code • 5. fields.fix_title: Inspect for vacuum leaks and check fuel trim data with a scan tool
fields.step_by_step_instructions: 1. Review short- and long-term fuel trim values by bank on a scan tool • 2. Smoke-test the intake for leaks matching the trending bank • 3. Repair any leak found • 4. Clear codes and recheck trims after a drive cycle

fields.fix_title: Clean throttle body and check MAF/MAP sensor readings
fields.step_by_step_instructions: 1. Clean the throttle body bore and blade of carbon buildup • 2. Compare MAF/MAP readings against expected values at idle and 2,500 RPM • 3. Address any sensor reading found out of spec • 4. Clear codes and monitor trim recovery

fields.fix_title: Diagnose fuel delivery imbalance affecting one bank
fields.step_by_step_instructions: 1. Compare fuel pressure and injector pulse width between banks • 2. Identify a restricted injector, filter sock, or fuel rail issue isolated to one bank • 3. Repair or replace the faulted component • 4. Clear codes and confirm trims converge between banks
